V11 / COMPLETE SCENE REVIEW

Every prediction. Every outcome.

46 labeled plume scenes and 152 reviewed no-plume scenes. Open any row to see the original image, saved prediction and annotation in three connected panes.

Open three-pane viewer ↗

Groups use native pixel overlap at the saved cutoff, 0.65.

How the groups work
  • Strong match: plume IoU at least 50%.
  • Partial match: plume IoU from 10% to below 50%.
  • Weak trace: some correct plume pixels, but IoU below 10%.
  • Missed plume: no correct plume pixels, even if there are marks elsewhere.
  • False alarm: a reviewed no-plume scene with any marked pixel.
  • Correct clear: a reviewed no-plume scene with no marked pixels.

IoU measures the area shared by prediction and annotation, divided by their combined area. A partial match is not a measured distance-based near miss. A correct clear scene does not prove zero methane.

02 / THE U-NET JUMPS

Better, with trade-offs.

The same 198 development scenes were scored for each run. Each model uses its own selected threshold.

v11 is not the highest F1 of these three. It was retained because it reduced false alarms while meeting the project's development checks.

THE TRADE-OFF

v8 → v11

same scenes
PrecisionHow much of the marked area matched a label
66.5%→71.5%
RecallHow much of the labeled plume was found
44.3%→42.2%
Clear scenes with a markOut of 152 reviewed no-plume scenes
23→18

Fewer false marks came with lower recall. The two thresholds differ; this is a development comparison, not a controlled independent test.

!

Still missing too much. v11 completely missed 19 of the 46 labeled plume scenes at its selected threshold. No model here is ready for a US-wide accuracy claim.

03 / BIGGER BASELINE

More real data. A stronger test.

The new MARS-based U-Net uses a larger, mixed Sentinel-2 and Landsat training set. Its results are not yet included in this snapshot.

Training started · 30 Oct

25,051 Sentinel-2 + 5,253 Landsat observations. MARS plume labels provide the supervised masks.

01
Training

30,304 observations used to fit the new model.

02
Selection

1,102 observations reserved for choosing a checkpoint.

03
Location holdout

60 observations: 20 plume and 40 no-plume, at locations held out from this model.

The held-out regions have been involved in earlier project work. This will test the new model on held-out locations, but it is not a completely untouched project-wide test. Only two of the held-out plume observations are in the US.

04 / RECENT WORK

What changed.

A visual timeline of the research and the tools supporting it.

OCT 23–24

Rebuilt the data path

Checked real pairs and labels, added clear scenes, and found that full-scene context and scene-centered inputs improved development traces.

OCT 25

Reduced false alarms

Replayed difficult clear training sites. v11 improved precision and reduced clear-scene activations, while recall remained a problem.

OCT 26

Checked outside models

Compared actual outputs from our U-Net and the released MARS model on the same reviewed scenes, including misses and false marks.

OCT 30

Started a larger baseline

Verified cached MARS files, moved large working data to D:, separated locations, and started a new 13.6M-parameter U-Net run.

05 / READ THIS WITH THE RESULTS

Progress is not deployment.

The plots show exposed development evidence. Plume masks are not emission-rate estimates, and a CAFO or oil facility nearby is not proof that it caused a plume.

01Inspect both successful and failed predictions.
02Check new locations and reviewed clear scenes.
03Measure source location and methane amounts only when supported by suitable labels.
